attachments.origin_landmark: perineal body and the median raphe of the bulb of the penis (or the perineal body in the female)
attachments.insertion_landmark: perineal membrane, corpus spongiosum and the dorsal aspect of the penis or clitoris

innervation.root_levels: S2-S4 (deep perineal branch of the pudendal nerve)

actions: empties the urethra at the end of micturition
assists erection by compressing the deep dorsal vein
contributes to the ejaculatory and orgasmic contractions

functional_compartments.name: Single fiber population
functional_compartments.function_note: In the female the two halves are separated by the vaginal orifice and act as a weak vaginal sphincter (sphincter vaginae). The bulbocavernosus reflex it mediates is the standard test of sacral reflex arc integrity after spinal cord injury.
functional_compartments.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed.; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed.; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

ultrasound_injection_approach.transducer_placement: Not routinely ultrasound-guided in the published literature: injections are placed submucosally/subcutaneously into the lateral aspect of the muscle via a transvaginal approach (women) or directly into the perineal body/bulb region (men), guided by palpation of the muscle belly and its midline raphe rather than by imaging.
ultrasound_injection_approach.depth_layer: Superficial perineal pouch, immediately deep to the vaginal introital mucosa (women) or perineal/scrotal skin overlying the bulb of the penis (men).
ultrasound_injection_approach.identification_cues: Palpated as a paired band either side of the vaginal introitus/perineal raphe; in women its tenderness and hypertonicity on digital exam is the indication for treatment (vaginismus/genito-pelvic pain-penetration disorder).
structures_at_risk: urethra, running deep and slightly anterior to the muscle in both sexes
vaginal mucosa (women) -- the injection route itself
perineal branches of the pudendal nerve, running with the muscle
ultrasound_injection_approach.notes: A real, comparatively well-studied target for genito-pelvic pain/penetration disorder and vaginismus, with several randomized placebo-controlled trials -- e.g. 20 U onabotulinumtoxinA bilaterally (Petersen et al.) and a repeated 50 U protocol (Haraldson et al.) into the bulbocavernosus/bulbospongiosus muscles for vestibulodynia, and submucosal 100-200 U regimens (Desai et al.; Helmi) for vaginismus. RCT results for pain outcomes have been mixed/negative on primary endpoints despite positive secondary measures (e.g. reduced intravaginal pressure, improved sexual function), recorded here as genuinely unresolved rather than settled. In men, 100 U onabotulinumtoxinA into the perineal body and bulbospongiosus improved short-term global response for chronic prostatitis/chronic pelvic pain syndrome in a small RCT (Gottsch et al.).
ultrasound_injection_approach.source: Karp BI, Stratton P (2025) Toxicon 258:108336, doi:10.1016/j.toxicon.2025.108336 -- review summarizing RCTs of bulbocavernosus/bulbospongiosus BoNT for genito-pelvic pain/penetration disorder and chronic prostatitis/pelvic pain syndrome, including Petersen, Haraldson and Gottsch et al. (PubMed); Desai SA, Shah B, Kroumpouzos G (2024) Int J Womens Dermatol 10(4):e186, doi:10.1097/JW9.0000000000000186 -- transvaginal submucosal technique for vaginismus (PubMed); Helmi ZR (2022) Rev Bras Ginecol Obstet 44(9):854-865, doi:10.1055/s-0042-1751287 -- injection sites/dose comparison (150 vs 200 U) for vaginismus (PubMed)
